semantics.layout: One integer n on its own line, followed by exactly n lines of two unsigned-decimal integers a_i,b_i. Positions distinct; rows need not be sorted. LF and original CRLF accepted.
semantics.uniqueOutput: Single integer, minimum destroyed original beacons. No custom, floating or multiple-valid-output checker needed.
semantics.activation: Inclusive leftward radius, never destroys itself, destroyed beacons do not activate. Added beacon chooses any suffix deletion (including none); its coordinate/power are not part of input or restricted by input bounds.

oracle.method: Sort by coordinate. S[i+1]=1+S[j], where j is number of earlier positions strictly less than a_i-b_i. Output n-max(S). S describes actual survivors of a prefix when its last beacon activates; it is not a freely selectable surviving subset.
oracle.complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary memory
oracle.argument: The added rightmost beacon destroys exactly a suffix, or none. For each retained prefix, its last beacon activates and deletes all predecessors at coordinates >=a_i-b_i; the untouched prefix then executes unchanged. Maximize survivors across all prefixes.
oracle.independentReference: For every retained prefix, mark destroyed indices by literal right-to-left activations and pairwise inclusive-distance tests; do not activate marked indices. Enumerate all suffix cutoffs, then minimize suffix deletions plus marked indices. No bisect or DP in this reference.

maxSizeReasoning: Each active dense unit beacon destroys its immediate predecessor; best survivor count is ceil(n/2).
All gaps exceed radius so no beacon is destroyed, even in reverse input order.
Every activation deletes all earlier beacons, leaving exactly one survivor.
Detached endpoint survives in addition to ceil(99999/2) dense-prefix survivors.
